extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: suspends a registered practitioner from practice before the USPTO, describes procedural service/publication steps, and directs compliance with duties and notices under applicable USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a State when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If no response is filed, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity and deadline to oppose (40-day response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must file any response opposing reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days of the Notice and Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order informs the respondent of the 40-day deadline and the specific regulatory grounds on which to oppose; failure to timely respond may result in a finding that there is no genuine issue of material fact and the imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reasons to oppose (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to reciprocal discipline must be grounded on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references § 11.24(d)(1) as the exclusive basis for contesting reciprocal discipline; the Notice and Order must inform the respondent of these available grounds for opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation citation: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis for action in this case is a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies the specific USPTO regulation violated as the legal predicate for the disciplinary action; the Order references the State orders on which this citation is predicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is appropriate, the USPTO will impose a suspension identical in substance and duration to that imposed by the State (here: two (2) years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the suspension term to match the State court's discipline and directs implementation effective as ordered by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made publicly accessible via the OED FOIA Reading Room; the Order directs electronic publication as part of the discipline process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette (Notice of Suspension content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension describing the respondent, registration number, violation citation, predicating state orders, and summary of factual misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice of Suspension must include the respondent's name, registration number, the regulation violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), references to the state orders, and a concise statement of the factual bases (e.g., unreasonable fee, failure to consult, improper commission, indemnity drafting, dishonesty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted and to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice requirement is to ensure other jurisdictions and courts are informed of the USPTO's disciplinary action and the underlying reasons; the Order directs such notice pursuant to § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties upon suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as a condition of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not recite § 11.58's text, it directs compliance with whatever duties that section prescribes (e.g., client notification, file transfer/retention, refunding unearned fees, and other post-suspension obligations).

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice cannot be delivered, publish the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Notice and Order cannot be delivered to the respondent, the Notice and Order shall be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order documents that the Notice and Order was not deliverable and therefore was published in the Official Gazette on specified dates; publication serves as constructive notice when direct delivery fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and Certificate of Service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must include a Certificate of Service showing mailing by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at addresses provided to the OED Director and other identified addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate of Service lists specific addresses used, notes certified mail and return receipt procedures, and documents service methods (including email when used) to establish proper service of the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings supporting reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The State orders' factual findings supporting suspension include: charging a corporate client an unreasonable fee; failing to consult with the client before paying a client's employee a $10,000 commission for assistance in securing representation; drafting an indemnity agreement for that employee contrary to the client's interests; and dishonesty related thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific misconduct findings are summarized in the Notice of Suspension as the factual underpinning for the State suspension and thus the USPTO's reciprocal discipline; they represent the professional conduct failures that justify suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact upon non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order applies this principle to conclude that, in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, reciprocal suspension is appropriate; non-response functions as a default for purposes of the § 11.24 analysis.
